executiveSummary: GM0938's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 18,460 residents, 14 neighbourhoods, five BAG places, 22 BRT settlements, two stations and four logical road-border links are internally coherent, and all ten presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Meerssen's severe local mechanisms are not municipality-average river and rain scalars: the official July 2021 analysis describes a coupled cross-border Geul-Maas event, Geul branches beneath roads/A2, a 76 m five-pipe siphon beneath the Julianakanaal whose capacity fell under high Maas backwater and blockage, and a low-lying Bunde-Brommelen-Westbroek 'bathtub' also exposed to groundwater and terrace runoff. The canonical river preset instead holds 2.535865 m from T+24 through T+72, grows affected population-equivalent from 10,644 to 10,906 and allocates 1,469 to upland Ulestraten at T+24. Pluvial T+24 emits 0.562700 m and 2,760 affected without rainfall, terrain, soils/groundwater, streams, buffers, sewer or receiving-water state, then clears direct effects by T+72 without evidence. Current Waterinfo provides three point observations and four Uikhoven forecasts only through T+24; none establishes the Geul, inundation, siphon/defence state or T+48/T+72. Public registers identify 61 water assets, Enexis/WML/Ziggo territories, one grid-planning area, 44 antennas, eight education locations and nearby MUMC+, but not live topology, capacity, backup, acceptance or restoration. A2/A79 links are duplicated corridor segments rather than four independent paths, Bunde's wastewater pump routes to Limmel and is under an ongoing renovation programme, and acute care/supply depend on Maastricht. Exact hazard, service and recovery claims must be suppressed or labelled synthetic until selected time-valid forcing and an auditable first-72-hour action/resource state exist; null, empty, stale and horizon-limited inputs remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0938 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0938 as Meerssen in Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Zuid, and report 18,460 residents, density 691/km², 28.9% aged 65 or older and 2,792 one-person households. The reference point [5.757237634940059,50.88289092175777] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Fourteen neighbourhoods in three districts sum exactly to 18,460 residents; published households total 8,510 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 5,340. Allocation preserves the municipal control without rewriting published cells.

Five active BAG places are Bunde, Geulle, Meerssen, Moorveld and Ulestraten. Twenty-two BRT labels comprise two buurtschappen, eight deelkernen, one gehucht and eleven woonkernen; these feature types are not interchangeable population controls. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District-heating and public-charging values are missing in all fourteen neighbourhoods and cars per household is missing twice. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero; annual residence omits commuters, school/care occupancy, tourists and transient A2/A79/airport users.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — July 2021 flooding and waterlogging in South Limburg: Geul system analysis
evidenceSources.edition: Final authority-commissioned analysis dated 26 April 2022; historical July 2021 scenario; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The historical event delivered about 128 mm averaged over the Geul catchment from 13–15 July 2021, mostly in Belgium; the estimated Valkenburg peak was about 135 m³/s, almost 90 m³/s from Belgium. It is official historical scenario evidence, not current forcing or universal calibration.

At Meerssen the Geul separates into Geul, Kleine Geul and Geulke, passes under local roads/A2 and then through a 76 m siphon of five parallel 2.5 m pipes beneath the Julianakanaal before reaching the Maas. Low terrain bounded by the canal dike creates a bathtub drained by streams/culverts and, under high Maas conditions, temporary pumping.

The 2021 Geul flow near Meerssen was estimated at 85–100 m³/s while the model calculated 110 m³/s; simultaneous Maas discharge exceeded 3,300 m³/s and raised the receiving level near NAP +44.1 m. Ideal siphon capacity near 85 m³/s fell to roughly 55 m³/s under Maas backwater, with driftwood/sediment and two weaker pipes further material to performance.

The report describes depths above 2 m and extensive flooding in Bunde, Brommelen and Westbroek, while cautioning that other events can be driven by high groundwater, terrace runoff or springs and require a detailed groundwater model. Its Meerssen high-flow gauge was unsuitable/inaccurate. Preserve event, datum, method and uncertainty; never transplant values to a new scenario.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Current Water in Balans projects and Meerssen water/sewer planning
evidenceSources.edition: Current project page inspected 3 September 2026; municipal Water Programme dated 7 September 2022; project updates through 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Meerssen's Water in Balans project lists phases 1 and 2 as completed and Landgoed Vliek/definitive-measures calculation as current, while the broader Geul-catchment programme remains source-to-mouth and involves Belgian authorities. Programme state is not live buffer volume, maintenance or event performance.

The 2022 municipal Water Programme treats the interaction of groundwater and surface water around Bunde, Geulle and Westbroek and persistent high groundwater as complex. The municipal kwelsloten/culvert map at https://www.meerssen.nl/projecten-en-themas/project/overzicht-kwelsloten-en-duikers covers only part of the July 2021 area and explicitly describes management state at the beginning of 2022, not current operation.

The current Bunde sewer-pump renovation page at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/projecten/renovatie-rioolgemaal-bunde/ says aged technical components are being replaced and wastewater is routed to Limmel. It plans continuity/site accessibility during works but supplies no live state, throughput, reserve, power/backup or completion evidence.

The 18 May 2026 Moorveldsberg/Heerenstraat project notice at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/actueel/nieuws/2026/werkzaamheden-moorveldsberg-geulle-start/ starts the first of four sewer/road phases. Project geography and start are current context; exact audit-time closure, emergency access and completion remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Time-scoped Bunde and Uikhoven water observations and forecasts
evidenceSources.edition: Observations valid 2 September 2026 17:30Z; forecasts retrieved 3 September 2026; Waterinfo CC0
supports: Three point observations are available: Bunde canal discharge 19.92 m³/s publisher-classed no-classification, Bunde canal level 4,406 cm NAP classed normal, and Uikhoven level 3,509 cm NAP classed normal. Point parameter/state does not establish the Geul, local inundation, siphon/defence function or municipality-wide safety.

Four forecasts cover only Uikhoven level at T+1/+6/+12/+24, each 3,498 cm NAP and publisher-classed reduced. No local Bunde forecast and no T+48/T+72 forecast exists; Uikhoven station naming/jurisdiction and point assignment must remain explicit.

Observation, forecast, historical scenario and synthetic output require distinct evidence classes. Retain station, coordinates, water body, parameter, unit/datum, issue/valid/retrieval time, quality and coverage; expire absent horizons to NoData rather than holding, extrapolating or translating normal/reduced into dry/safe.
The four forecast records cannot validate a generic 2.535865 m municipality flood depth or an unchanged T+24–T+72 state.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Crisisplan, high-water plan consultation, care warning process and 72-hour guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Crisisplan 2024–2027; RBP Hoogwater 2026–2029 consultation closed 26 August 2026 but definitive adoption not confirmed; current guidance inspected 3 September; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The current crisis plan supports scalable and prolonged crisis working plus international cooperation. The renewed high-water plan consultation at https://www.vrzl.nl/actueel/vernieuwd-rampbestrijdingsplan-hoogwater-ter-inzage distinguishes regional-system high water, Maas high water and defence-failure/polder effects and adds an Impact Analysis Team; definitive adoption was not confirmed at audit time.
GHOR's post-2021 process alerts the care network as standard from GRIP 2. This is a governance trigger, not evidence that a particular alert was sent, received, acknowledged or acted upon.

Current https://app.zuidlimburgveilig.nl/veiligheidsthemas/blijf-72-uur-veilig guidance recommends three litres of water per person per day, food, medication, lighting/communications and a household plan for 72 hours. Guidance is not a household stock, warning-reach or self-reliance observation.

No reviewed public input supplies incident-valid IAT/GRIP decision, warning receipt, evacuation/reception, Geul/Maas control action, pump/resource assignment, care acceptance, logistics delivery or confirmed completion.

evidenceSources.publisher: Nationaal Wegenbestand / ProRail / public-transit publishers / Gemeente Meerssen
evidenceSources.title: E06 — A2/A79, rail, transit and historically demonstrated access dependency
evidenceSources.edition: NWB January 2026, ProRail 2025, GTFS/reference snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; NWB and ProRail CC0; publisher-specific GTFS terms vary
supports: Four logical road links represent two A2 edges toward Beek and Maastricht and two A79 edges toward Maastricht and Valkenburg. Each pair shares one physical road reference and its repeated nominal 260-unit ceilings are consecutive/non-additive, not independent redundant capacity.

Two stations, Bunde and Meerssen, and 28 GTFS stop areas provide geometry/schedule context only. They do not establish current trains/buses, platform/access state, emergency priority, passenger/freight/supply throughput or T+72 operation.

A municipal notice at https://www.meerssen.nl/nieuws_en_bekendmakingen/actueel/afrit_51_%28bunde_meerssen%29_in_zuidelijke_richting_afgesloten records closure of A2 exit 51 Bunde/Meerssen southbound during the July 2021 flood. This is a historical mechanism/action test, not a current closure.
The graph contains Dutch reference geometry only and cannot represent upstream Belgian Geul response state. Zero bounded NDW records never means roads, crossings, rail or transit are open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, provider territories, grid planning, communications and education context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY version unspecified; exact NBNL/RDI licences not established in consumed metadata
supports: The HWH clip contains 61 realized records: two sewer pumps, five surface-water pumps and 54 weirs. Sixty capacity values are null; one emergency-pumping record at Geulle aan de Maas reports 1,250 without a displayed comparable unit/connectivity in the consumed schema.

A centre-point lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas, WML water and Ziggo media, all last-updated 7 September 2025; drainage is empty. Territory identifies a provider, not customer/asset topology or live availability.

One postcode/grid-planning sample links to Limmel and reports withdrawal/injection queues and eleven projects whose earliest date is 2027. Planning/nameplate data are not current Meerssen load, spare capacity, outage or restoration.

RDI returns 44 antenna sites and DUO eight education locations. Counts/locations do not establish backhaul/power/coverage, emergency communications, shelter designation, opening, occupancy, staffing or supplies.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Nearest acute-care registration and regional dependency
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1 published 3 July 2026, CC0; current facility pages inspected 3 September
supports: No acute hospital is registered inside GM0938. The nearest listed facility from the municipal centre is Maastricht UMC+ at 6.14 km, with 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric functions, 24 reported treatment rooms and 23,000 reported 2025 visits; Zuyderland Heerlen is 15.49 km away.

Facility role, straight-line distance and annual values do not establish route travel time, current acceptance/diversion, occupancy, staffing, utilities, oxygen/medicines, backup endurance or surge capacity.

Meerssen care continuity is therefore cross-boundary and shares A2/A79/local-access, telecom, utility and supply dependencies with Maastricht and the wider region. Annual registration must not create a local operational Facilities percentage.

No reviewed public source supplies live ambulance distribution, care-home evacuation ability, hospital access/acceptance, generator/fuel, oxygen/blood/medicine stock or T+72 restoration; use authorized aggregates only.
